claims.text: Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi is a single-phase FCC alloy in the baseline state.
Equiatomic CrCoNi is a single-phase FCC derivative of CrMnFeCoNi.
Reducing Mn content forms CrCoNi from CrMnFeCoNi.
Rolling followed by controlled annealing can be used to promote nanotwin formation in CrCoNi.
Favorable magnetic ordering in CrCoNi can drive an FCC-to-HCP transformation triggered by dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries.
Cryogenic deformation makes nanotwinning a more prominent deformation mode in these alloys.
An intermediate annealing regime is required because excessive annealing would erase the desired structure while insufficient annealing would suppress dynamic recovery and twin nucleation.
Processed CrCoNi develops a dense network of deformation-induced nanotwins.
CrCoNi contains nanoscale HCP regions associated with deformation and internal boundaries.
Nanotwins impede dislocation motion and increase strength while still permitting strain accommodation.
Removing Mn reduces magnetic frustration relative to Mn-containing CrMnFeCoNi and restores an energetic preference for HCP over FCC in CrCoNi.
The FCC-to-HCP transformation can increase strength without compromising plastic deformation.
Nanotwinning and the magnetically driven FCC-to-HCP transformation cooperate synergistically to improve mechanical performance.
Processed CrCoNi should have higher yield and ultimate tensile strengths than similarly processed CrMnFeCoNi while maintaining or slightly improving ductility.
The mechanical-property improvement should be more pronounced at cryogenic temperature because both twinning and transformation become more active.
The proposed mechanism applies broadly to Cr-based multicomponent alloys with reduced or absent Mn.
The mechanism should not apply when processing suppresses twinning or the FCC-to-HCP transformation, such as after extremely high-temperature annealing.
The magnitude of the property improvements and the processing conditions needed to activate the proposed synergy remain quantitatively uncertain.
Identically processed CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi specimens tested at room and cryogenic temperatures provide a controlled comparison of microstructure, magnetic ordering, strength, and ductility.

Failure to observe both enhanced nanotwinning and an FCC-to-HCP transformation in CrCoNi, together with failure to observe a statistically significant strength increase without ductility loss, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: CrCoNi is described as a reduced-Mn derivative produced by reducing Mn, but converting equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi to equiatomic CrCoNi requires removal of both Mn and Fe, so the stated compositional intervention is incomplete.
